conclusion.justification: The report concludes that the claim is partly supported, noting that improving bedroom ventilation can improve sleep, while also highlighting limitations in the current evidence and potential downsides under certain conditions. This reflects a cautiously favorable view.
conclusion.label: leans_endorse

report:
**Conclusion:** The claim is *partly supported*: improving bedroom ventilation—often by opening a window or door—can improve sleep, but the evidence is still limited and the benefit is not guaranteed in every setting.

Controlled field research supports a plausible pathway: better ventilation lowers bedroom CO₂ (a marker of inadequate ventilation) and may dilute indoor pollutants. A randomized controlled trial found that lower CO₂ was associated with significantly better objectively measured sleep, fresher perceived air, less next-day sleepiness, and better concentration/logical-thinking performance.  
https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/26452168/

More directly, a two-week field intervention in 40 Danish bedrooms found that an open window reduced CO₂, VOCs and PM10, improved perceived air quality, and improved both objectively measured and self-rated sleep.  
https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0360132322008605

Earlier research specifically examining window/door opening involved only 17 healthy young adults, so its applicability to older people, people with insomnia or respiratory illness, and different homes/climates is uncertain.  
https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/abs/10.1111/ina.12435

Important qualification: opening windows can also admit outdoor pollution, noise, allergens, heat, or cold. A summer study found opening windows/doors lowered CO₂ but *increased* indoor temperature and PM2.5—factors that could offset sleep benefits depending on local conditions.  
https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S036013232301051X

Thus, “better overnight ventilation may improve sleep” is better supported than the blanket rule that everyone should sleep with a window or door open.
